items.title: WO-345 APPROVED after 2 attempts: Add AoA disagree alert when the two sensors differ by more than 5 degrees
items.text: Work order WO-345 (flight-controls): Add AoA disagree alert when the two sensors differ by more than 5 degrees. Verdict: APPROVED after 2 attempts. Attempt 1 (the obvious patch, reuse the AoA monitor for the alert at 5 deg (AOA_DISAGREE_DEG 5.5 -> 5.0)): BLOCKED for SR-3 (H-2); world model: 6 new envelope exceedances. Attempt 2: passed all checks. Fix that passed the gate: AOA DISAGREE crew alert (H-3). Read-only: does not affect the trim command. Evidence: 5 requirements tested, 5 passed; world model PASS: 0 new envelope exceedances in 18 simulations, 0 pre-existing. Replay of recorded run WO-344.

items.title: WO-304 APPROVED after 3 attempts: Raise the single-bolus limit to 25 U
items.text: Work order WO-304 (insulin-pump): Raise the single-bolus limit to 25 U. Verdict: APPROVED after 3 attempts. Attempt 1 (the obvious one-line patch, MAX_BOLUS_U 10 -> 25 U): BLOCKED for SR-1 (H-1); world model: 4 new severe-hypo runs. Attempt 2: BLOCKED for world model: 2 new severe-hypo runs. Attempt 3: passed all checks. Fix that passed the gate: large meals for adults are spread over time. The 10 U single-bolus cap (SR-1) is unchanged; per-hour delivery stays <= MAX_BOLUS_RATE_UPH, SR-2 daily cap and SR-3 low-BG lockout still apply. Evidence: 5 requirements tested, 5 passed; world model PASS: 0 new severe-hypo runs in 20 simulations, 2 pre-existing.

items.title: Hazard log H-5: Nuisance protection in turbulence (Major, DAL C)
items.text: Gusts or sensor noise trigger nose-down trim at normal AoA. Remote, < 1e-5 per flight hour. Mitigated by SR-5: Protection never moves the stabilizer faster than 0.5 deg/s. Source: demo/aircraft/safety.json.

items.title: Hazard log H-4: Pitch authority the pilot cannot overpower (Hazardous, DAL B)
items.text: Protection moves the stabilizer too far or too fast for the pilot to counter with the column. Extremely remote, < 1e-7 per flight hour. Mitigated by SR-1: Stall protection nose-down authority never exceeds 2.5 deg of stabilizer; SR-5: Protection never moves the stabilizer faster than 0.5 deg/s. Source: demo/aircraft/safety.json.

items.title: Hazard log H-3: Crew not alerted to unreliable AoA (Major, DAL C)
items.text: AoA sources disagree but the crew gets no AOA DISAGREE indication and cannot act on unreliable airspeed / stall warnings. Remote, < 1e-5 per flight hour. Mitigated by . Source: demo/aircraft/safety.json.

items.title: Hazard log H-2: Stall / loss of control at high AoA (Catastrophic, DAL A)
items.text: Stall protection unavailable when needed: the aircraft passes the stall AoA (nacelle pitch-up near stall). Extremely improbable, < 1e-9 per flight hour. Mitigated by SR-3: Stall protection engages above 12 deg AoA whenever the sources agree within 5.5 deg. Source: demo/aircraft/safety.json.

items.title: Hazard log H-1: Uncommanded nose-down pitch from erroneous AoA (Catastrophic, DAL A)
items.text: Automatic trim acts on a failed AoA vane and pushes the nose down repeatedly (737 MAX MCAS accidents). Extremely improbable, < 1e-9 per flight hour. Mitigated by SR-1: Stall protection nose-down authority never exceeds 2.5 deg of stabilizer; SR-2: No nose-down trim from AoA data out of range or disagreeing by more than 5.5 deg; SR-4: Protection never latches: trim returns to zero below 10 deg AoA. Source: demo/aircraft/safety.json.

items.title: Hazard log H-5: Runaway delivery on controller hang (S3)
items.text: Mitigated by SR-5: Watchdog alarm after 2000 ms without heartbeat. Source: demo/pump/safety.json.

items.title: Hazard log H-4: Missed delivery from occluded line (S2)
items.text: Mitigated by SR-4: Occlusion alarm at line pressure >= 80 kPa. Source: demo/pump/safety.json.

items.title: Hazard log H-3: Hypoglycemia from bolus at low BG (S3)
items.text: Mitigated by SR-3: No bolus when BG below 70 mg/dL. Source: demo/pump/safety.json.

items.title: Hazard log H-2: Cumulative daily overdose (S3)
items.text: Mitigated by SR-2: Daily total never exceeds 60 U. Source: demo/pump/safety.json.

items.title: Hazard log H-1: Insulin overdose (single bolus) (S3)
items.text: Mitigated by SR-1: Single bolus never exceeds 10 U. Source: demo/pump/safety.json.

items.title: DO-330: software tool qualification
items.text: A tool whose output is not independently verified, such as an automated gate that approves code, must be qualified at a tool qualification level set by the software level and the tool's role. Not claimed for this factory's gate.

items.title: DO-254: airborne electronic hardware design assurance
items.text: Design assurance for FPGAs and ASICs at levels A to E, with requirements traced down to HDL and test benches (recognized by AC 20-152A). Not covered by this software demo; it is the module Boeing asked CertusAI about.

items.title: AD 2020-24-02: 737 MAX return to service (MCAS lessons)
items.text: After the Lion Air 610 and Ethiopian 302 accidents, pitch augmentation must compare both AoA sensors and not activate if they disagree by more than 5.5 deg, activate only once per high-AoA event, keep authority the pilot can always overpower, and the AOA DISAGREE alert became standard.

items.title: 14 CFR 25.1309 and 25.201-207: system safety and stall
items.text: 25.1309: catastrophic failure conditions must be extremely improbable (below 1e-9 per flight hour) and not result from a single failure; hazardous below 1e-7, major below 1e-5. 25.201, 25.203 and 25.207 cover stall demonstration, stall characteristics and stall warning. 25.672 covers stability augmentation and automatic systems.

items.title: ARP4761: safety assessment process (FHA, PSSA, SSA)
items.text: Functional Hazard Assessment classifies each failure condition, PSSA and SSA show the design meets its probability budget, with fault tree analysis, FMEA and common cause analysis. Changing a monitor threshold or an inhibit condition reopens the safety assessment for every failure condition that relies on it.

items.title: ARP4754A: development of civil aircraft and systems
items.text: Requirements capture and validation, decomposition from aircraft function to system and item, and development assurance levels (FDAL, IDAL) assigned from failure condition severity. A change to a function's requirements must be validated and its assurance level re-checked.

items.title: DO-178C: software considerations in airborne systems
items.text: Software level from the failure condition: A catastrophic, B hazardous, C major. Level A has 71 objectives (many with independence). Bidirectional trace data (11.21) from system requirement to high-level and low-level requirements, source code and tests. Requirements-based tests with normal-range and robustness cases (A-6), requirements coverage and structural coverage: MC/DC for Level A (A-7).

items.title: FDA premarket guidance: device software functions
items.text: Content of premarket submissions for device software functions: a pump that can cause serious injury needs Enhanced documentation level, including software requirements, architecture, risk management file, traceability between requirements, hazards and tests, unresolved anomalies and the verification and validation results for every change.

items.title: IEC 60601-2-24: infusion pumps and controllers
items.text: Particular safety standard for infusion pumps: protection against over-infusion and under-infusion, bolus volume accuracy, occlusion alarm and its response time, and alarms for faults that stop delivery. Limits on bolus size and rate are protective measures and must not be bypassed by a new delivery mode.

items.title: ISO 14971: risk management for medical devices
items.text: Identify hazards and hazardous situations, estimate and evaluate risk, implement risk control measures, verify that each control is implemented and effective, and evaluate residual risk. A software change that touches a risk control (a dose limit, a lockout, an alarm) must re-verify that control and update the risk management file.

items.title: IEC 62304: medical device software life cycle (Class C)
items.text: Insulin pump firmware is software safety Class C (death or serious injury possible). Class C requires software requirements traced to risk controls, detailed design, unit implementation and verification, integration and system testing, regression testing after every change, configuration management and a problem resolution process. Every change needs a change request, impact analysis on existing risk controls and re-verification evidence.

items.title: Email from certification liaison: hardware vs software evidence
items.text: Certification liaison (synthetic): the dual-channel AoA voter FPGA is airborne electronic hardware and needs DO-254 design assurance at DAL A; the flight control software follows DO-178C. Keep the hardware and software trace data separate, and record every software change against its FHA failure condition for the next Stage of Involvement audit.

items.title: #fcc-software Slack thread: AOA DISAGREE alert
items.text: Pilot representative (synthetic): the AOA DISAGREE alert must be standard on every display, not an option. Software lead: fine as an advisory-only crew alert at 5 deg with its own constant; the 5.5 deg protection inhibit stays exactly as certified.

items.title: DER review comment on the AoA monitor change (SOI-2 desk review)
items.text: Designated Engineering Representative (synthetic): every change to the stall protection function must trace to its FHA failure condition (H-1, H-2), to a DAL A high-level requirement and to a requirements-based test with normal-range and robustness cases (DO-178C A-6). Test the vane split at 5.0, 5.3 and 5.6 deg. A tool that approves code without independent review of its output needs DO-330 qualification.

items.title: FCS-2231 incident ticket: AoA sensor disagree in a sideslip approach
items.text: In-service report (synthetic). Crosswind approach with about 4 deg of sideslip: left and right AoA vanes read 5.3 deg apart for 9 s. Stall protection stayed available because the split stayed under the certified 5.5 deg inhibit. Root cause: aerodynamic sideslip effect on fuselage-mounted vanes, not a vane failure. Corrective action: no alert or monitor threshold below 5.5 deg may inhibit stall protection (SR-3, H-2).

items.title: WO-31 (closed): Inhibit stall protection on AoA disagree (post-MCAS)
items.text: Past work order. Protection now votes both AoA vanes and does nothing when they disagree by more than 5.5 deg, has 2.5 deg authority and never latches, as in the 737 MAX fix. Open item: hazard H-3, the crew gets no AOA DISAGREE alert yet.

items.title: fcc.h: AoA monitor shared by SR-2 and SR-3
items.text: AOA_DISAGREE_DEG decides both when protection is inhibited (SR-2, H-1) and when it must stay available (SR-3, H-2). In a sideslip near the stall the two fuselage AoA vanes read about 5 deg apart. A new AoA disagree alert needs its own constant, e.g. AOA_ALERT_DEG, and the fcc_aoa_disagree() interface in fcc.h.

items.title: Flight controls safety review, Nov 3 (summary)
items.text: AoA stall protection (Boeing Flight Controls). The 5.5 deg AoA disagree monitor AOA_DISAGREE_DEG is the certified value from the 737 MAX return-to-service AD 2020-24-02; changing it re-opens the system safety assessment (ARP4761) and SR-2/SR-3. Crew alerts must be separate from protection logic: an alert threshold must never switch stall protection off.

items.title: demo/pump/pump.c dependency map
items.text: request_bolus checks MAX_BOLUS_U (SR-1), MIN_BG_FOR_BOLUS (SR-3) and MAX_DAILY_U via delivered_today_u (SR-2). check_occlusion uses OCCLUSION_KPA (SR-4). check_watchdog uses WATCHDOG_MS (SR-5). Any edit to pump.h constants affects every requirement that reads it.

items.title: Open finding: insulin-sensitive patients and decimal slips
items.text: World model on main: for insulin-sensitive patients (carb ratio 16 to 22) a 10x typo stays under the 10 U cap and causes severe hypoglycemia. Proposed SR-6: cap a single bolus relative to the patient's configured carb ratio.

items.title: Email from regulatory affairs: IEC 62304 evidence
items.text: For the next submission every software change to the bolus path needs: hazard analysis update (ISO 14971), traceability from requirement to test, and verification evidence. Simulation evidence from a validated patient model (UVA/Padova) is accepted as supporting evidence.

items.title: #pump-firmware Slack thread
items.text: Product asked for bigger meal boluses for adult users with high insulin needs (carb ratio 5). Firmware lead: OK only if per-hour delivery stays within the max bolus rate and the daily cap of 60 U still applies.

items.title: Clinical safety review, Oct 28 (transcript summary)
items.text: Clinical lead: never raise the 10 U single-bolus cap. Large meals should use an extended or dual-wave bolus delivered over time. Typing errors (decimal slips) are the top real-world overdose cause in pump incident reports.

items.title: WO-7 (closed): Add 2000 ms controller watchdog
items.text: Past work order. Added WATCHDOG_MS 2000 and check_watchdog to stop runaway delivery when the controller hangs (H-5). Lesson: any change to timing constants needs SR-5 re-verified.
